text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Kidneys and blood pressure: creatinine with eGFR (CKD-EPI 1910), urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio and urinalysis with microscopy, electrolytes and bicarbonate, uric acid, calcium, phosphate and PTH, blood count, HbA1c and a lipid panel once; the earlier insurance creatinine obtained; ultrasound of the kidneys and liver; standardized office blood pressure at every visit and home readings
  • Nephrology consultation to confirm the stage and cause of the kidney disease and advise on blood pressure, an SGLT2 inhibitor, medicines for alcohol use disorder at his kidney function, and pain relief
  • Losartan 50 mg daily from intake, raised to the maximum tolerated dose, with potassium and creatinine two to four weeks after each start or change, accepting a rise in creatinine of up to 30 percent; less salt
  • Alcohol: AUDIT, DSM-5-TR criteria and PEth with consent; liver tests and FIB-4; a withdrawal-risk score (PAWSS) and outpatient withdrawal with a five-day chlordiazepoxide taper, daily telephone checks and thiamine; addiction-focused counseling with the clinic's addiction medicine team each week and mutual-help meetings if he wishes; PEth and liver tests at follow-up
  • Medicine for alcohol use disorder: naltrexone 50 mg daily, which needs no dose change at his kidney function, with liver tests and a wallet card about opioid blockade; acamprosate not chosen because it needs a lower dose at his creatinine clearance and is avoided below 30 mL/min, and he could not reliably take it three times a day
  • Liver: ultrasound and vibration-controlled transient elastography for an indeterminate FIB-4; abstinence as the treatment
  • SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin 10 mg daily) once he has been abstinent for some weeks and is eating regularly, because heavy drinking and fasting raise the risk of ketoacidosis; held on days he cannot eat or drink, with potassium and creatinine two to four weeks after starting, accepting an early fall in eGFR
  • Pain and medicine safety: no naproxen, ibuprofen or other oral anti-inflammatory medicines; acetaminophen up to 2,000 mg a day; no opioids or tramadol with kidney disease and in early recovery, and none at all if naltrexone is started; any new medicine checked for kidney dosing
  • Safety: a structured safety assessment, firearms locked with ammunition apart, small supplies of withdrawal medicine, a written safety plan, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, and safety review at every visit
  • Work and recovery: keep the morning writing hours from nine to eleven; replace the late-morning drink with a swim or a ride; no alcohol kept in the writing room; PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at intake and follow-up
  • Tobacco: advice to stop, with nicotine replacement or varenicline offered when he is ready

resource.title: Jack London synthetic care plan
resource.description: Alcohol use disorder with chronic kidney disease and hypertension in a working writer: a 39-year-old novelist who writes a thousand words every morning on his ranch comes in tired, with swollen ankles, and is found to have a blood pressure of 158/98, an eGFR of 43 and albumin in the urine, and to drink heavily. The episode covers the AUDIT, the DSM-5-TR criteria and PEth; liver tests, FIB-4 and elastography; outpatient withdrawal management with a withdrawal-risk score and thiamine; medicine for alcohol use disorder chosen with kidney function in mind (naltrexone, with acamprosate needing a lower dose at his creatinine clearance and avoided below 30 mL/min); CKD staging by KDIGO 1913 with eGFR and urine albumin, the cause (hypertension and two years of daily naproxen, without stones or gout), ultrasound, the kidney failure risk equation and mineral tests; blood pressure under KDIGO 1910 and the 1914 AHA/ACC guideline with an angiotensin receptor blocker at the maximum dose and potassium and creatinine checks; an SGLT2 inhibitor once he is abstinent, because heavy drinking raises the risk of ketoacidosis; analgesic and opioid safety, with no NSAIDs, a lower acetaminophen limit and naltrexone's opioid blockade; the safety assessment and lethal-means counseling; tobacco; vaccinations in kidney and liver disease; and a plan that protects his morning writing hours.

code.text: Kidneys and blood pressure: creatinine with eGFR (CKD-EPI 1910), urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio and urinalysis with microscopy, electrolytes and bicarbonate, uric acid, calcium, phosphate and PTH, blood count, HbA1c and a lipid panel once; the earlier insurance creatinine obtained; ultrasound of the kidneys and liver; standardized office blood pressure at every visit and home readings

Nephrology consultation to confirm the stage and cause of the kidney disease and advise on blood pressure, an SGLT2 inhibitor, medicines for alcohol use disorder at his kidney function, and pain relief

Losartan 50 mg daily from intake, raised to the maximum tolerated dose, with potassium and creatinine two to four weeks after each start or change, accepting a rise in creatinine of up to 30 percent; less salt

Alcohol: AUDIT, DSM-5-TR criteria and PEth with consent; liver tests and FIB-4; a withdrawal-risk score (PAWSS) and outpatient withdrawal with a five-day chlordiazepoxide taper, daily telephone checks and thiamine; addiction-focused counseling with the clinic's addiction medicine team each week and mutual-help meetings if he wishes; PEth and liver tests at follow-up

detail.description: Guideline reference: GL-APA-AUD-2018, GL-SUD-2021, GL-ASAM-AWM-2020, GL-AASLD-NIT-2025

code.text: Medicine for alcohol use disorder: naltrexone 50 mg daily, which needs no dose change at his kidney function, with liver tests and a wallet card about opioid blockade; acamprosate not chosen because it needs a lower dose at his creatinine clearance and is avoided below 30 mL/min, and he could not reliably take it three times a day
Liver: ultrasound and vibration-controlled transient elastography for an indeterminate FIB-4; abstinence as the treatment

SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin 10 mg daily) once he has been abstinent for some weeks and is eating regularly, because heavy drinking and fasting raise the risk of ketoacidosis; held on days he cannot eat or drink, with potassium and creatinine two to four weeks after starting, accepting an early fall in eGFR

Pain and medicine safety: no naproxen, ibuprofen or other oral anti-inflammatory medicines; acetaminophen up to 2,000 mg a day; no opioids or tramadol with kidney disease and in early recovery, and none at all if naltrexone is started; any new medicine checked for kidney dosing

Safety: a structured safety assessment, firearms locked with ammunition apart, small supplies of withdrawal medicine, a written safety plan, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, and safety review at every visit

Work and recovery: keep the morning writing hours from nine to eleven; replace the late-morning drink with a swim or a ride; no alcohol kept in the writing room; PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at intake and follow-up
Tobacco: advice to stop, with nicotine replacement or varenicline offered when he is ready
